label: Chad McIntosh, Over 100 Arguments for the…: A wholly contingent thing is a thing with no necessary…
locator: original presentation PDF pp.9–26: p.20, argument #10 Koons, D
interpretation: This is the displayed definition, not a proof that ordinary modal contingency is equivalent to having no necessary parts. It supplies neither a contingent population nor a wholly contingent aggregate. The later claim that a contingent thing has a wholly contingent part is a separate substantive reading. Attribution is to McIntosh’s presentation only, not the unread Koons1997 or Hawthorne–Cortens1993 works referenced on p24. No formal result or premise truth is established.
